Top story. Iran Keeps Hormuz Strait Closed as US Deal Expires

Iran kept the Strait of Hormuz closed on Monday as a sixty-day agreement with Washington lapsed without a broader deal. Shipping traffic through the waterway slowed to a third of its normal volume and marine insurers widened exclusion zones across the Gulf. Tanker owners diverted vessels toward the Red Sea, adding nine days to routes bound for Rotterdam.

Ebola Outbreak in Congo Becomes Deadliest on Record

Health officials in the Democratic Republic of Congo confirmed the outbreak is now the deadliest recorded, with cases spreading beyond the initial province for the first time since March. Damaged roads have slowed the response, leaving three treatment centres without power. The health ministry said burial teams reached fewer than half of reported deaths last week.

Zambia President Hichilema Wins Second Term with 60 Percent

Zambia's electoral commission declared President Hakainde Hichilema the winner of a second term, taking sixty percent of the vote on a turnout of just under half the register. Opposition parties said they would challenge the results in three provinces, citing delays in transmitting tallies from rural districts. Observers from the African Union reported no violence.
